title: Run frozen claim-evidence retrieval holdout
description: Operator-approved execution of EXP-0006. Freeze independently authored source questions and acceptable evidence sets before treatment; build a disposable claim-evidence projection over completed MAP tasks with exact Markdown-section or code-symbol anchors, source hashes and time watermarks, and separate positive-proof and negative-boundary channels; compare against the recorded TASK-262 capsule baseline. Preserve existing TASK-260 through TASK-262 artifacts and production retrieval unchanged. This is experiment evidence only, not production integration or authority.
objective: Measure whether disposable claim-addressed evidence units improve exact and historically correct proof retrieval beyond the 18/20 capsule baseline without changing production retrieval or canonical authority.
forbidden_changes: Do not modify TASK-260 through TASK-262 scripts, tests, reports, or frozen result artifacts.
Do not integrate the experiment into production retrieval, startup, routing, UI, task authority, or canonical policy.
Do not add embeddings, external services, a learned reranker, or a knowledge graph.
Do not author treatment against evaluation questions before the holdout is independently frozen.
expected_artifacts: Independent frozen holdout and evaluator notes
Disposable claim-evidence pilot and focused tests
Machine-readable results plus a plain-English experiment report
reviewer_role: Independent reviewer who did not implement the treatment and verifies frozen-label provenance, metrics, boundaries, hashes, and absence of production integration.
risk: Treatment leakage, authority duplication, false positives from negative-boundary text, mistaking a current file hash for historical evidence, or overclaiming from a small MAP-specific holdout.
acceptance_criteria: An independent helper freezes fresh source questions, acceptable evidence sets, and explicit negatives before the treatment is authored; a different helper evaluates blinded results after implementation.

The pilot derives disposable claim-evidence units with exact Markdown heading or code symbol anchors, proof role, source hash, and time watermark; positive proof and negative boundaries are indexed and scored separately and never act as authority.

The evaluation reports task recall, exact-source and anchored-evidence accuracy, abstention behavior, historical-version correctness, acceptable substitutes, packet size, authoring cost, and parser coverage against the recorded 18/20 capsule and 12/12 task-recall baselines.

Focused tests cover unit extraction, claim-card validation, positive-versus-boundary isolation, deterministic ranking, source-hash drift, acceptable evidence sets, and abstention; existing TASK-260 through TASK-262 candidate hashes and artifacts remain unchanged.
The report records pass, revise, or park without production integration, embeddings, a learned reranker, a full knowledge graph, canonical policy changes, or automatic promotion.
